from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vector spaces follow eight formal axioms.", "Closure ensures results stay within the space.", "Associativity and commutativity simplify calculations."]
        self.setup_layout("The Eight Axioms: Defining the Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define axioms
        axioms = VGroup(*[Text(f"Axiom {i+1}", font_size=24, color=WHITE) for i in range(8)])
        # Grid positions for axioms
        positions = ["A1", "A3", "A5", "C1", "C3", "C5", "E1", "E3"]
        for i, axiom in enumerate(axioms):
            self.place_at_grid(axiom, positions[i], scale_factor=0.8)
            self.play(Write(axiom), run_time=0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(FadeIn(VGroup(*axioms)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        # Highlight closure (Axiom 1 & 2)
        self.play(axioms[0].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"), axioms[1].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        # Highlight associative/commutative (Axiom 3, 4)
        self.play(axioms[2].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"), axioms[3].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Abstract spaces are sets with rules.",
            "Feature spaces drive modern machine learning.",
            "Abstraction enables powerful predictive mathematical tools."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Summarize concepts in bullet points #FFFFFF
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Visual representation: Abstract set with rules (Venn-like or Set notation)
        abstract_set = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE),
            Dot(color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.2),
            Dot(color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.2+LEFT*0.3),
            Dot(color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.2+RIGHT*0.3)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(abstract_set, 'B2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(abstract_set))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash key takeaways in #FFD700
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Visual representation: ML Feature space (dots in high dimensional-like cluster)
        ml_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=YELLOW_D) for _ in range(10)])
        ml_dots.arrange_in_grid(2, 5, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(ml_dots, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(ml_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display final application graphic #40E0D0
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#40E0D0"))
        
        # Visual representation: Predictive tool (Arrow/Chart icon)
        final_arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#40E0D0")
        self.place_at_grid(final_arrow, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(GrowArrow(final_arrow))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: From Concrete to Abstract: The Shift
sections.content: Review prerequisite (standard 2D/3D vectors). Introduce the idea that vectors aren't just arrows, but objects that follow specific 'rules of engagement' (addition and scalar multiplication).
sections.example: Visual: An arrow (v) transforms into a function (f(x)) and a 2x2 matrix, both following the same vector addition rules.

sections.title: The Eight Axioms: Defining the Space
sections.content: Introduce the formal structure of a Vector Space (V) over a field (F). Focus on closure, associativity, commutativity, identity, and inverses.
sections.example: A 'Robot Logic' checklist: If two states are combined (Addition) and scaled (Multiplication), do they remain in the original 'Robot World' (Closure)?

sections.title: Non-Traditional Examples: Beyond Arrows
sections.content: Demonstrate that unusual sets can be vector spaces if they obey the 8 axioms. This highlights the power of abstraction.
sections.example: The 'Polynomial Garden': Showing that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 behaves exactly like vectors in 3D space, represented by coordinates [a, b, c].

sections.title: Visualization: Mapping Abstract Spaces
sections.content: Explain how abstract spaces can be visualized via 'isomorphism'—mapping complex abstract structures onto familiar 3D grids.
sections.example: Animation: A sound wave (complex) being mapped onto a coordinate grid representing frequency amplitudes, showing how abstract spaces help us solve real-world signal problems.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap: An abstract vector space is a 'set with rules'. Application: Why this matters for Machine Learning (feature spaces) and Quantum Physics.
sections.example: A neural network character 'classifying' different animal features as vectors in a high-dimensional space, proving that abstraction leads to powerful predictive tools.
